selected_primary_idea.title: TraceRes: A Task-Specific Resolution Passport for Credible Optical Nanoscopy
selected_primary_idea.summary: A cross-modality evidence record that converts a nominal super-resolution result into a task-specific, calibratable, and falsifiable structural claim.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Optical microscopy resolution claims for known structural tasks.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Typed resolution objective + declared information channel + multi-term error budget + blinded calibration + bounded status.
falsification_conditions: Typed passports do not reduce localization-versus-structure misclassification.
The multi-term lower bound does not improve calibration on truth-known cases.
Independent audits do not detect fewer omitted alternatives or artifact pathways.
Passport-constrained modality choice does not improve valid-information yield at matched resource budget.

competitive_ideas.title: Adaptive modality selector
competitive_ideas.reason: Useful downstream optimizer but needs TraceRes validation semantics.

competitive_ideas.title: Mechanism taxonomy map
competitive_ideas.reason: Useful explanatory component but insufficient as a measurement-validation contribution.

rejected_ideas.title: Image-sharpening score
rejected_ideas.reason: Visual sharpness does not establish structural resolution or coordinate accuracy.

evolution_trace.change: Recast a universal limit question into a task-specific inference question.
Combine resolution taxonomy with calibration, sampling, and artifact records.
Add blinded counterfactual cases and bounded statuses.
